checks.finding: No ambiguity meeting the four-part evidence gate was found. Terms/states/inputs (e.g., the check-id identifier grammar ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$, the capability-derived trigger fragment shape, the three-state disabled-legacy/advisory/required handling, the command-discovery contract's fixed package.json-then-scripts/<id>-pair order) are each defined concretely enough that two implementers would converge on the same behavior.

No direct conflict found among requirements, acceptance criteria, constraints, or non-goals. The package documents a completed 14-finding adversarial review (Blockers B1-B7, Majors M1-M3, Minor) plus a follow-on adversarial final verification (M3, NEW-01, B5) with each ruling cross-referenced consistently across REQ-001..REQ-006, Edge Cases, Field Definitions, Security Boundaries, and acceptance-tests.md's AC/TEST rows; I independently checked several of the most revision-heavy areas (REQ-002's two-input-state exit-code contract, REQ-004 Step 2a/2b Block ordering, REQ-005's single-Block-mechanism claim) and found each self-consistent.

requirements.md Edge Cases ('v1 Registry, field absent entirely...') and AC-030 both state that a zero-matched-Capability resolve under active capability_enforcement produces a present, schema-valid, empty-array Capability Summary that lite-gate must treat as a legitimate pass-through (baseline-five-checks-only, no VERDICT: FAIL) -- distinct from the absent-Summary FAIL case. But acceptance-tests.md's TEST-030 (the only test row cited against AC-030) exercises only the absent-Summary FAIL condition ('no capability-summary.yaml at all is VERDICT: FAIL'); no AC/TEST row (checked TEST-002, TEST-004, TEST-011, TEST-015/016, TEST-026, TEST-030, and REQ-006 fixtures a-l) verifies the present-but-empty-Summary pass-through behavior. This is exactly the absence-vs-legitimate-empty-content confusion Blocker [B6] was raised to fix, so a future implementer/test-suite author working from acceptance-tests.md alone has no fixture guarding against regressing into that same defect. This is a Phase 1 acceptance-criteria gap fixable only in acceptance-tests.md, not a design/implementation matter, so it belongs to this gate; Major per calibration's 'missing observable acceptance criterion' bucket.

requirements.md's Assumptions section (4 bullets) explicitly flags cross-epic risk rather than silently resolving it: A5's Pending status and its provisional field-naming/aggregation-rule reliance are marked for mandatory re-check if A5 changes before this feature's own implementation; lite-gate/SKILL.md's unprotected status is marked for re-verification at implementation-start time rather than assumed permanent. Risks section restates the same items with explicit resolution triggers.

Human-approval/governance boundaries are in scope and testable: AC-024 makes the Spec-Review-Status/Impl-Review-Status Pending-until-human-approval boundary directly inspectable; AC-010/AC-031 make the protected-file human-copy governance boundary (ADR-0011 pattern) testable via a three-way exact-set/hash/post-copy-verification contract for a to-be-authored feature-scoped runner, with the existing Epic-136 runner's inapplicability documented (investigation.md INV-019) rather than left silently assumed.

Every prior open question (OQ-001/002/003) is resolved concretely and normatively in requirements.md's own REQ text (not deferred to design), every REQ cites the sibling-epic contract it wires to, and the package underwent and closed a documented adversarial review plus follow-on verification. The one gap I found (EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE) is a missing acceptance-test row, not a missing product-behavior decision a design reviewer would need to invent -- the behavior itself (present-empty Summary = pass-through) is already stated in AC-030's own text, only the corresponding test assertion is absent.
